# Midnight Sun (Zara Larsson album)
**Midnight Sun** is the fifth studio album by Swedish singer and songwriter Zara Larsson, released on 26 September 2025 through her own label, Sommer House, and Epic Records . Arriving just seven months after her fourth studio album, *Venus* (2024), and following her holiday extended play, *Honor the Light* (2023), *Midnight Sun* represents a prolific period in Larsson's career, marking a deliberate thematic shift from the winter-focused melancholia of her previous EP to the euphoric, relentless energy of the Scandinavian summer .

Developed primarily throughout 2024 and 2025, the album sees Larsson reuniting with her frequent creative partner MNEK, who serves as the project's executive producer alongside Larsson herself . The record also features significant contributions from producers Margo XS and Zhone, as well as songwriter Helena Gao . Musically, *Midnight Sun* is an electropop and dance-pop record that deeply integrates elements of drum and bass, Eurodance, and house music, reflecting a sonic palette designed to evoke the "never-ending" daylight of the Nordic summer .

Upon its release, *Midnight Sun* garnered widespread critical acclaim, achieving a Metacritic score of 89, indicating "universal acclaim" . Critics praised the album's cohesive production, Larsson's vocal agility, and the maturation of her songwriting, which balances commercial viability with introspective themes of ambition, identity, and the astrological concept of the "Saturn return" . The album was supported by three singles: "Pretty Ugly", "Midnight Sun", and "Crush" . The title track, "Midnight Sun", earned Larsson her first Grammy Award nomination for Best Dance Pop Recording at the 68th Annual Grammy Awards .

Commercially, the album debuted at number one in Sweden, marking Larsson's third chart-topping release in her home country . It also achieved top-ten placement in Norway and top-forty positions in the United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia . In the United States, it debuted at number 3 on the Top Dance/Electronic Albums chart, a career high in that specific genre chart . To promote the album, Larsson embarked on the **Midnight Sun Tour**, commencing in Europe in October 2025, following a supporting slot on Tate McRae's **Miss Possessive Tour** in North America .

## Background and Career Context
### Post-*Venus* Independence
Following the release of *Venus* in February 2024, Zara Larsson had firmly established her independence within the music industry through the creation of her own record label, Sommer House, licensed to Epic Records . This structural change allowed Larsson greater autonomy over her release schedule, resulting in a rapid succession of projects that defied the traditional multi-year gap between pop album cycles *Venus* had been a commercial stabilizer, reaching number three in Sweden and producing hits like "Can't Tame Her" and "On My Love" with David Guetta . However, Larsson sought to create a project that felt more conceptually unified and representative of her personal evolution as she approached her late twenties .

In late 2023, Larsson released *Honor the Light*, a Christmas EP that explored the "winter" aspect of her Swedish heritage . The EP was commercially successful, topping the Swedish charts, but it also sparked a creative counter-reaction in Larsson . Having explored the dark, cozy, and melancholic atmosphere of the Swedish winter, she felt compelled to document the opposing extreme: the Swedish summer . This duality became the foundational concept for *Midnight Sun*, serving as a sonic and thematic sequel to the winter EP, completing a seasonal cycle in her discography .

### Conception and Title
The title *Midnight Sun* was chosen to encapsulate the album's prevailing mood: an intense, relentless brightness that refuses to fade . In interviews, Larsson explained that the meteorological phenomenon of the midnight sun—where the sun remains visible 24 hours a day in the Arctic Circle during summer—served as a perfect metaphor for the "manic happiness" and high-energy anxiety she wanted the music to convey . She stated, "I wanted the whole album to feel like it's a summer night and it never ends... A part of my soul is a Swedish summer night. This record encompasses that, how life is so beautiful it makes you cry" .

The concept extended beyond geography to represent Larsson's stage in life. At 27 years old during the album's release, Larsson was navigating her "Saturn return," an astrological transit associated with adulthood, restructuring, and long-term decision-making . The "midnight sun" thus also represented a spotlight on her identity, where "all sides" of her personality—"lovestruck, wistful, ambitious, cocky, flippant, and uncertain"—were exposed without the cover of darkness .

## Recording and Production
### Creative Team and Process
Unlike her previous albums *So Good* (2017) and *Poster Girl* (2021), which utilized a vast array of songwriters and producers from different "writing camps," *Midnight Sun* was crafted by a tight-knit core team . The primary collaborator was Uzoechi "MNEK" Emenike, a long-time creative partner who had previously worked with Larsson on her breakthrough international hit "Never Forget You" . MNEK served as the album's executive producer, co-writing and producing the majority of the tracks .

Joining MNEK were producer Margo XS and songwriter Helena Gao . This small circle allowed for a more "stream of consciousness" approach to the songwriting, with Larsson noting that the process felt reminiscent of her early days making EPs, where the focus was on "having fun and just creating and speaking honestly" rather than chasing radio trends . The team worked in various studios, including sessions in Stockholm and Los Angeles, but a pivotal period of the album's development occurred during a trip to Jamaica . During these sessions, the team focused on rhythm and groove, which, while eventually filtered through a European electropop lens, gave the album its rhythmic vitality .

### Philosophy: "Touching Grass"
A driving philosophy behind the recording process was the concept of "touching grass"—a Gen Z slang term for disconnecting from the internet and reconnecting with reality . Larsson, who had spent nearly two decades in the public eye and was known for her active (and occasionally controversial) social media presence, sought to ground the album in physical sensations . She told *The Line of Best Fit*, "Midnight Sun is literally about touching grass... It's the most amazing thing. And the small things, too. Feeling the wind. Listening to a good song when you're driving. That's the essence and the core of who I am right now" .

This desire for tangibility influenced the production choices. The synthesizers, while digital, were tuned to feel "warm" and "atmospheric," and the tempos were set to mimic the heart-racing feeling of anxiety or excitement . The inclusion of specific cultural references, such as the voice of reality star Tiffany Pollard on "Hot & Sexy", was done not just for meme potential, but to anchor the album in the specific pop culture reality Larsson inhabits .

## Musical Style and Aesthetics
### Sonic Palette
*Midnight Sun* is characterized by its high-tempo energy and "kaleidoscopic pop" sound . Critics have categorized the album as electropop and dance-pop, but with distinct sub-genre influences that separate it from the R\&B-leaning pop of *So Good* or the disco-pop of *Poster Girl*.1

* **Drum and Bass:** Several key tracks, including "Blue Moon" and the title track "Midnight Sun", utilize drum and bass (DnB) breakbeats . This influence nods to the genre's resurgence in the mid-2020s and provides a frantic, driving energy that contrasts with Larsson's melodic, often ethereal vocal delivery . 
* **Euro-Trance and House:** The album embraces its European roots through "Eurosummer" sounds—a blend of late 90s/early 2000s trance synthesizers and house music beats . Tracks like "Hot & Sexy" feature the "four-on-the-floor" kick drums characteristic of house music, while "Eurosummer" explicitly references the continent's dance heritage . 
* **Synth-Pop:** The production relies heavily on "polished pop production" and "glistening dance pop" textures . The synths are often described as "starry-eyed" or creating an "underwater dreamscape," contributing to the album's immersive quality .

### Visual Identity
The visual aesthetic of *Midnight Sun* was meticulously curated to match the sonic themes. Larsson described the look as "Y2K Malibu Barbie," citing fashion from Versace (2003) and Dior (2005) as primary inspirations . This aesthetic blends "chiffon, light materials that blow in the wind" with "shiny chain skirts," aiming to evoke a specific era of early 2000s hedonism mixed with Swedish nature .

To further cement this nostalgic visual identity, Larsson collaborated with **Lisa Frank**, the artist known for her psychedelic, neon-colored school supply designs that defined 90s and Y2K childhoods . A limited-edition CD version of the album featured custom artwork by Frank, depicting an "underwater dreamscape full of dolphins, flowers, and musical notes" . This collaboration highlighted the album's playful, colorful, and "unserious" side .

## Themes and Lyrics
Lyrically, *Midnight Sun* is described as Larsson's most personal work, moving beyond generic love songs to explore themes of autonomy, female solidarity, and the anxieties of aging in the pop industry .

### Ambition and The "Saturn Return"
A recurring motif in the album is the tension between ambition and burnout. The track "The Ambition" addresses the relentless drive required to maintain a career in the music industry, with Larsson discussing how "endlessly chasing success can be draining" . This is paired with "Saturn's Return", a song titled after the astrological event that occurs around age 29\. In this track, Larsson reflects on her past attempts to "control all that was unknown" and her eventual acceptance of uncertainty . These songs provide an introspective counterweight to the album's uptempo production, offering a glimpse into the pressure Larsson feels as a "20-year veteran" of the industry at only 27 .

### Modern Romance and Sexuality
While the album contains love songs, they are framed through a lens of modern confidence and agency. "Crush" and "Blue Moon" explore the giddy, "hopeless romantic" phase of new love, but tracks like "Hot & Sexy" and "Puss Puss" present a more assertive, sexually liberated persona . In "Hot & Sexy", Larsson collaborates with Tiffany Pollard (via samples/vocals) to create a campy, self-assured anthem about desirability "Puss Puss" is described as "cheeky" and "deliciously honest," blending sexual confidence with a sense of humor .

### Female Solidarity
The song "Girl's Girl" explicitly tackles the media narrative that pits female pop stars against one another . Larsson explained in interviews that she wanted to write about the "warmth between women in pop," rejecting competition in favor of support . The lyrics navigate the complexity of loyalty—specifically the scenario of finding a friend's partner attractive but choosing the friendship over the flirtation—ultimately affirming the bond between women .

## Songs
### Track-by-Track Analysis
1\. "Midnight Sun" 
The title track opens the album with "upbeat, electro-pop energy" . It introduces the album's central metaphor of light that never fades. The production blends a driving beat with atmospheric synths, and the song was critically acclaimed for its "Swedish-tinged production" . A remix featuring American R\&B singer Muni Long was released to broaden the track's appeal . 
2\. "Blue Moon" 
Described as an "anthem for the hopeless romantics," this track features a "heart-racing drum 'n' bass" beat . The juxtaposition of the rapid percussion with Larsson's smooth, longing vocals creates a sense of urgency and emotional vulnerability . 
3\. "Pretty Ugly" 
Released as the lead single, "Pretty Ugly" is a bass-heavy track that explores the "ugly moments" of life and relationships . It serves as a sonic bridge between the rhythmic pop of Venus and the electronic focus of Midnight Sun. 
4\. "Girl's Girl" 
A mid-tempo pop track focused on friendship. It was praised for its conversational tone and relatable subject matter regarding loyalty and the rejection of male-centered competition . 
5\. "Crush" 
A "glistening dance pop" song that became a radio favorite . It captures the simple, euphoric feeling of a new crush, with a production that critics noted for its "laser focus" on commercial appeal . 
6\. "Eurosummer" 
This track serves as a thematic anchor, explicitly referencing the European summer lifestyle. It incorporates elements of trance and Eurodance, making it a "euphoric" festival anthem . It was written with Mary Weitz and features production by Zhone . 
7\. "Hot & Sexy" 
A house-influenced track that stands out for its campy, bold attitude . It features uncredited vocals from reality TV icon Tiffany Pollard, adding a layer of internet-culture relevance . The song is described as "genre-bending" and purely hedonistic . 
8\. "The Ambition" 
One of the album's few downtempo moments, this track offers a "slow tempo" that allows for lyrical introspection . It details the exhaustion of the music industry and the personal cost of Larsson's drive . 
9\. "Saturn's Return" 
The penultimate track is a "serious and introspective" ballad set against a celestial production backdrop . Larsson sings about growing up and the realization that control is an illusion, marking a significant maturation in her songwriting . 
10\. "Puss Puss" 
The album closes with this high-energy track. It begins with a spoken-word intro mimicking a phone call to a boyfriend before exploding into a dance beat . It serves as a confident, fun sign-off, reinforcing the album's theme of "unapologetic" fun .

## Release and Promotion
The promotional campaign for *Midnight Sun* was designed to maximize the "endless summer" theme, utilizing both digital engagement and traditional touring.

### Singles
* **"Pretty Ugly"** (25 April 2025): The lead single, introducing the era's visual and sonic shift . 
* **"Midnight Sun"** (13 June 2025): The title track, which became a top-five hit in Sweden and garnered a Grammy nomination . 
* **"Crush"** (15 August 2025): The final pre-release single, which performed well on pop radio formats .

### Media and Events
Larsson hosted an **iHeartRadio Album Release Party** on 29 September 2025, where she performed the new material and participated in a Q\&A hosted by JoJo . She also appeared on popular podcasts, including *The Zach Sang Show*, where she discussed the album's creation and her viral "dolphin" meme associated with the song "Symphony" . Additionally, she appeared on the UK podcast *Saving Grace* with GK Barry .

### Touring
Larsson employed a two-phase touring strategy. In the summer of 2025 (August–September), she joined Canadian singer Tate McRae as the opening act for the North American leg of the **Miss Possessive Tour**.1 This exposed her to McRae's similar demographic of young, dance-pop fans.

Following the album's release, Larsson launched her own headline tour, the **Midnight Sun Tour**. The tour began in Europe in October 2025, with dates in cities such as Munich, Vienna, and Berlin . The North American leg of the tour was scheduled for February through April 2026, with major stops including the Kia Forum in Los Angeles .

## Critical Reception
*Midnight Sun* was met with "universal acclaim" from music critics . On Metacritic, the album holds a score of **89** out of 100, based on 4 reviews .

* **Rolling Stone** hailed it as her "most radiant body of work," praising the visible growth in her artistry . 
* **Vogue** declared that with this album, "Larsson is finally coming into view as pop's main girl" . 
* **The FADER** called the album "a testament to the uncanny moment the Swedish pop star has found herself in," noting the "refreshingly unserious" nature of tracks like "Hot & Sexy" . 
* **Clash** praised the album's focus, stating Larsson was "honing in on what she does best with laser focus: starry-eyed, joyous Scandi-pop" . 
* **Nylon** and **W Magazine** highlighted the "glistening dance pop" production and Larsson's vocal flexibility . 
* **The Brown Daily Herald** provided a more tempered but positive review, noting that while the "Malibu Barbie" aesthetic was fun, the deeper cuts like "Saturn's Return" provided necessary weight to the project .

## Commercial Performance
Sweden and Scandanavia 
In Sweden, Midnight Sun debuted at number 1 on the Sverigetopplistan, cementing Larsson's dominance in her home market . It was her fourth project to top the chart (including her EPs and albums) . In Norway, the album debuted at number 10 on the VG-lista, and in Denmark, it reached number 33.1 
International Markets 
In the United Kingdom, the album debuted at number 36 on the Official Albums Chart, maintaining her presence in one of her historically strongest markets . In Germany, it peaked at number 18, a significant improvement over her previous album Venus which had peaked at number 71.1 
In the United States, *Midnight Sun* debuted at number **119** on the *Billboard* 200 . While a modest entry on the all-genre chart, it found significant success in the dance sector, debuting at number **3** on the Top Dance/Electronic Albums chart . It also reached number 22 on the Top Album Sales chart .

Streaming 
The album generated over 4 million streams globally in its first 24 hours . By October 2025, Larsson's total career streams had surpassed 10.5 billion, a milestone aided by the influx of listeners from the new album .

Lisa Frank is an artist known for her psychedelic, neon-colored school supply designs that defined 90s and Y2K childhoods.
A limited-edition CD version of Midnight Sun featured custom artwork by Lisa Frank.
The custom artwork by Lisa Frank depicted an "underwater dreamscape full of dolphins, flowers, and musical notes".
This collaboration highlighted Midnight Sun's playful, colorful, and "unserious" side.
Lyrically, Midnight Sun is described as Zara Larsson's most personal work.
Midnight Sun moves beyond generic love songs to explore themes of autonomy, female solidarity, and the anxieties of aging in the pop industry.
A recurring motif in Midnight Sun is the tension between ambition and burnout.
The track "The Ambition" addresses the relentless drive required to maintain a career in the music industry.
In "The Ambition", Zara Larsson discusses how "endlessly chasing success can be draining".
"The Ambition" is paired with "Saturn's Return".
"Saturn's Return" is a song titled after the astrological event that occurs around age 29.
In "Saturn's Return", Zara Larsson reflects on her past attempts to "control all that was unknown".
In "Saturn's Return", Zara Larsson reflects on her eventual acceptance of uncertainty.
These songs provide an introspective counterweight to Midnight Sun's uptempo production.
These songs offer a glimpse into the pressure Zara Larsson feels as a "20-year veteran" of the industry at only 27.
While Midnight Sun contains love songs, they are framed through a lens of modern confidence and agency.
"Crush" and "Blue Moon" explore the giddy, "hopeless romantic" phase of new love.
Tracks like "Hot & Sexy" and "Puss Puss" present a more assertive, sexually liberated persona.
In "Hot & Sexy", Zara Larsson collaborates with Tiffany Pollard (via samples/vocals) to create a campy, self-assured anthem about desirability.
"Puss Puss" is described as "cheeky" and "deliciously honest", blending sexual confidence with a sense of humor.
The song "Girl's Girl" explicitly tackles the media narrative that pits female pop stars against one another.
Zara Larsson explained in interviews that she wanted to write about the "warmth between women in pop", rejecting competition in favor of support.

The lyrics of "Girl's Girl" navigate the complexity of loyalty—specifically the scenario of finding a friend's partner attractive but choosing the friendship over the flirtation—ultimately affirming the bond between women.
The title track "Midnight Sun" opens the album with "upbeat, electro-pop energy".
"Midnight Sun" introduces the album's central metaphor of light that never fades.
The production of "Midnight Sun" blends a driving beat with atmospheric synths.
The song "Midnight Sun" was critically acclaimed for its "Swedish-tinged production".
A remix of "Midnight Sun" featuring American R&B singer Muni Long was released to broaden the track's appeal.
"Blue Moon" is described as an "anthem for the hopeless romantics".
"Blue Moon" features a "heart-racing drum 'n' bass" beat.
The juxtaposition of the rapid percussion with Zara Larsson's smooth, longing vocals in "Blue Moon" creates a sense of urgency and emotional vulnerability.
"Pretty Ugly" was released as the lead single.
"Pretty Ugly" is a bass-heavy track that explores the "ugly moments" of life and relationships.
"Pretty Ugly" serves as a sonic bridge between the rhythmic pop of Venus and the electronic focus of Midnight Sun.
"Girl's Girl" is a mid-tempo pop track focused on friendship.
"Girl's Girl" was praised for its conversational tone and relatable subject matter regarding loyalty and the rejection of male-centered competition.
"Crush" is a "glistening dance pop" song that became a radio favorite.
"Crush" captures the simple, euphoric feeling of a new crush.
The production of "Crush" was noted by critics for its "laser focus" on commercial appeal.
The track "Eurosummer" serves as a thematic anchor, explicitly referencing the European summer lifestyle.
"Eurosummer" incorporates elements of trance and Eurodance, making it a "euphoric" festival anthem.
"Eurosummer" was written with Mary Weitz.
"Eurosummer" features production by Zhone.
"Hot & Sexy" is a house-influenced track that stands out for its campy, bold attitude.
"Hot & Sexy" features uncredited vocals from reality TV icon Tiffany Pollard.
The song "Hot & Sexy" is described as "genre-bending" and purely hedonistic.
"The Ambition" is one of the album's few downtempo moments.
The track "The Ambition" offers a "slow tempo" that allows for lyrical introspection.
"The Ambition" details the exhaustion of the music industry and the personal cost of Zara Larsson's drive.
The penultimate track "Saturn's Return" is a "serious and introspective" ballad set against a celestial production backdrop.
In "Saturn's Return", Zara Larsson sings about growing up and the realization that control is an illusion.
"Saturn's Return" marks a significant maturation in Zara Larsson's songwriting.
The album closes with the high-energy track "Puss Puss".
"Puss Puss" begins with a spoken-word intro mimicking a phone call to a boyfriend before exploding into a dance beat.
"Puss Puss" serves as a confident, fun sign-off, reinforcing the album's theme of "unapologetic" fun.
"Pretty Ugly" was released on 25 April 2025.
"Pretty Ugly" is the lead single, introducing the era's visual and sonic shift.
"Midnight Sun" was released on 13 June 2025.
The title track "Midnight Sun" became a top-five hit in Sweden.
The title track "Midnight Sun" garnered a Grammy nomination.
"Crush" was released on 15 August 2025.
"Crush" is the final pre-release single.
"Crush" performed well on pop radio formats.
Zara Larsson hosted an iHeartRadio Album Release Party on 29 September 2025.
At the iHeartRadio Album Release Party, Zara Larsson performed the new material and participated in a Q&A hosted by JoJo.
Zara Larsson appeared on popular podcasts, including The Zach Sang Show.
On The Zach Sang Show, Zara Larsson discussed the album's creation and her viral "dolphin" meme associated with the song "Symphony".
Zara Larsson appeared on the UK podcast Saving Grace with GK Barry.
Zara Larsson employed a two-phase touring strategy.
In the summer of 2025 (August–September), Zara Larsson joined Canadian singer Tate McRae as the opening act for the North American leg of the Miss Possessive Tour.
Joining Tate McRae's tour exposed Zara Larsson to McRae's similar demographic of young, dance-pop fans.
Following the album's release, Zara Larsson launched her own headline tour, the Midnight Sun Tour.
The Midnight Sun Tour began in Europe in October 2025, with dates in cities such as Munich, Vienna, and Berlin.
The North American leg of the Midnight Sun Tour was scheduled for February through April 2026.
Major stops on the North American leg of the Midnight Sun Tour include the Kia Forum in Los Angeles.
Midnight Sun was met with "universal acclaim" from music critics.
On Metacritic, Midnight Sun holds a score of 89 out of 100, based on 4 reviews.
Rolling Stone hailed Midnight Sun as Zara Larsson's "most radiant body of work".
Rolling Stone praised the visible growth in Zara Larsson's artistry on Midnight Sun.
Vogue declared that with Midnight Sun, "Larsson is finally coming into view as pop's main girl".
The FADER called Midnight Sun "a testament to the uncanny moment the Swedish pop star has found herself in".
The FADER noted the "refreshingly unserious" nature of tracks like "Hot & Sexy" on Midnight Sun.
Clash praised Midnight Sun's focus, stating Zara Larsson was "honing in on what she does best with laser focus: starry-eyed, joyous Scandi-pop".
Nylon and W Magazine highlighted the "glistening dance pop" production of Midnight Sun.
Nylon and W Magazine highlighted Zara Larsson's vocal flexibility on Midnight Sun.
The Brown Daily Herald provided a more tempered but positive review of Midnight Sun.
The Brown Daily Herald noted that while the "Malibu Barbie" aesthetic of Midnight Sun was fun, the deeper cuts like "Saturn's Return" provided necessary weight to the project.
In Sweden, Midnight Sun debuted at number 1 on the Sverigetopplistan.
Midnight Sun cemented Zara Larsson's dominance in her home market of Sweden.
Midnight Sun was Zara Larsson's fourth project to top the Swedish chart (including her EPs and albums).
In Norway, Midnight Sun debuted at number 10 on the VG-lista.
In Denmark, Midnight Sun reached number 33.
In the United Kingdom, Midnight Sun debuted at number 36 on the Official Albums Chart.
Midnight Sun maintained Zara Larsson's presence in one of her historically strongest markets, the United Kingdom.
In Germany, Midnight Sun peaked at number 18.
Midnight Sun's peak at number 18 in Germany is a significant improvement over Zara Larsson's previous album Venus which had peaked at number 71.
In the United States, Midnight Sun debuted at number 119 on the Billboard 200.
While a modest entry on the all-genre chart, Midnight Sun found significant success in the dance sector.
Midnight Sun debuted at number 3 on the Top Dance/Electronic Albums chart.
Midnight Sun reached number 22 on the Top Album Sales chart.
Midnight Sun generated over 4 million streams globally in its first 24 hours.
By October 2025, Zara Larsson's total career streams had surpassed 10.5 billion.
The influx of listeners from the new album Midnight Sun aided Zara Larsson's total career streams surpassing 10.5 billion.

**Zara Maria Larsson** (Swedish:[[ˈsɑ̂ːra ˈlɑ̌ːʂɔn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Swedish "Help:IPA/Swedish")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/a/a2/Sv-Zara_Larsson.ogg/Sv-Zara_Larsson.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sv-Zara_Larsson.ogg "File:Sv-Zara Larsson.ogg"); born 16 December 1997) is a Swedish singer. She first rose to prominence in 2008 after winning the [second season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talang_2008 "Talang 2008") of _[Talang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talang\_(Swedish\_TV\_show) "Talang (Swedish TV show)")_, the Swedish version of the _[Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Got\_Talent "Got Talent")_ format. She later attained international recognition with singles including "[Lush Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lush_Life_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Lush Life (Zara Larsson song)")" (2015), "[Never Forget You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Forget_You_(Zara_Larsson_and_MNEK_song) "Never Forget You (Zara Larsson and MNEK song)")" (2015), and "[Ruin My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruin_My_Life_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Ruin My Life (Zara Larsson song)")" (2018).

In 2012, Larsson signed with the record label [TEN Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEN_Music_Group "TEN Music Group") and subsequently released her debut [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play"), _[Introducing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Introducing\_(EP) "Introducing (EP)"),_ in January 2013. The EP was supported by Larsson's first original single, "[Uncover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncover_(song) "Uncover (song)")", which charted at number one in Sweden and Norway, being certified [6× Platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") in the former.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-UMS_Platinum-1) Her debut studio album, _[1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "1 (Zara Larsson album)")_, followed in 2014.

Following her early success in Scandinavia, Larsson signed a three-year contract with [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records") in the United States. Her debut international album and second overall, _[So Good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So\_Good\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "So Good (Zara Larsson album)"),_ was commercially successful and was released in March 2017. Larsson's third studio album, _[Poster Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poster\_Girl\_(album) "Poster Girl (album)"),_ followed four years later in March 2021. Her fourth studio album, _[Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "Venus (Zara Larsson album)")_, was released on 9 February 2024. Larsson's fifth studio album, _[Midnight Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Sun\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "Midnight Sun (Zara Larsson album)")_, was released on 26 September 2025 to widespread [critical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_journalism "Music journalism") acclaim, while the album's [title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_Sun_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Midnight Sun (Zara Larsson song)") earned Larsson her first [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award "Grammy Award") nomination for [Best Dance Pop Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Dance_Pop_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Dance Pop Recording").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-2)

Zara Maria Larsson[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-3) was born on 16 December 1997 in [Solna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solna_Municipality "Solna Municipality"), [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_County "Stockholm County"), to Agnetha and Anders Larsson.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Svenska_Dagbladet-5) In an interview with _[Svenska Dagbladet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svenska\_Dagbladet "Svenska Dagbladet")_, she said that she was born "dead" due to a lack of oxygen from a [nuchal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuchal_cord "Nuchal cord").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Svenska_Dagbladet-5) Larsson grew up in [Tallkrogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallkrogen "Tallkrogen") in [Enskede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enskede_(locality) "Enskede (locality)"), south of Stockholm. Her mother is a [nursing assistant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unlicensed_assistive_personnel "Unlicensed assistive personnel") and her father is an officer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-6) She has a sister, Hanna, who is three years younger and is a singer and member of the band Lennix.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-7)

Her first primary school was the [Gubbängsskolan](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gubb%C3%A4ngsskolan "sv:Gubbängsskolan"); she transferred to the [Royal Swedish Ballet School](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kungliga_Svenska_Balettskolan "sv:Kungliga Svenska Balettskolan") in third grade.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Standard.co.uk-8) She attended the secondary school [Kulturama](https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kulturama "sv:Kulturama"), an art school in Stockholm.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-9) She has cited [Carola Häggkvist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carola_H%C3%A4ggkvist "Carola Häggkvist") and [Whitney Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") as early inspirations. She has said that since the age of five she knew that she wanted to become "immortal" like [Elvis Presley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elvis_Presley "Elvis Presley").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-2015_summer_speech-10)

### 2008–2011: Career beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zara_Larsson&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2008–2011: Career beginnings")]

[![Image 2: Young girl with blond hair holding a microphone](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/Zara_Larsson_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Zara_Larsson_%28cropped%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zara_Larsson_(cropped).jpg)

Larsson singing on [Sommarkrysset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sommarkrysset "Sommarkrysset") in 2008

Larsson won the [2008 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talang_2008 "Talang 2008") of _[Talang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talang\_(Swedish\_TV\_show) "Talang (Swedish TV show)")_,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-11) the Swedish adaptation of _[Got Talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Got\_Talent "Got Talent")_, at the age of 10,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-12) winning 500,000 [kronor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swedish_krona "Swedish krona").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-tv4-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-14) "[My Heart Will Go On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My_Heart_Will_Go_On "My Heart Will Go On")", the song she sang in the final, originally sung by [Celine Dion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celine_Dion "Celine Dion"), was later released that year as Larsson's debut single, charting at the official Swedish Singles Chart, [Sverigetopplistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sverigetopplistan "Sverigetopplistan"), for six consecutive weeks and peaking there at number seven for one week.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-15) She started singing on _[Sommarkrysset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sommarkrysset "Sommarkrysset")_ ("The Summer Cross"), another Swedish TV program.

Between December 2009 and January 2010, Larsson participated in a reality TV series called _Jag ska bli stjärna_ (English: "I shall become a star") where she and other young Swedish talents got help on the difficult road to international fame and success. She was managed by [Laila Bagge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laila_Bagge "Laila Bagge"), and they flew to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") in the United States where they visited and talked with [Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney "Disney") and the three big record label companies - [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"), [Sony Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music"), and [Warner Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Music_Group "Warner Music Group") - but she did not get a contract offer anywhere, which Larsson later attributed to her age at that time.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-2015_summer_speech-10)

### 2012–2014: Commercial success with _1_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zara_Larsson&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2012–2014: Commercial success with 1")]

[![Image 3: Blonde-haired woman sings into a microphone on stage in a sequined shirt](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/Zara_Larsson_Upptr%C3%A4der_P%C3%A5_Sommarkrysset_2013_By_Daniel_%C3%85hs_Karlsson_%282%29.jpg/250px-Zara_Larsson_Upptr%C3%A4der_P%C3%A5_Sommarkrysset_2013_By_Daniel_%C3%85hs_Karlsson_%282%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zara_Larsson_Upptr%C3%A4der_P%C3%A5_Sommarkrysset_2013_By_Daniel_%C3%85hs_Karlsson_(2).jpg)

Larsson singing on [Sommarkrysset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sommarkrysset "Sommarkrysset") in 2013

Larsson signed with [TEN Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEN_Music_Group "TEN Music Group") in 2012 to record her debut compilation recording.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-16) The recording, the [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP) _[Introducing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Introducing\_(EP) "Introducing (EP)")_, was leaked on 9 December 2012 through an unofficial music video of "[Uncover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncover_(song) "Uncover (song)")" on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube"), a static-view video featuring her singing the whole song in the recording studio in one whole continuous take.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-17) The five-song EP was released in Scandinavia on 21 January 2013, consisting exclusively of original songs.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-18) "Uncover" was released as the EP's lead single. It peaked at number one on both the [Sverigetopplistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sverigetopplistan "Sverigetopplistan") and [DigiListan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DigiListan "DigiListan") charts,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-swedishcharts1-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-SWE-20) as well as reaching number one in Norway and peaking at number three in Denmark,[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-NOR-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-den-22) and by 25 February 2013, the song was certified platinum in Sweden by [Universal Music Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Universal_Music_Group_labels "List of Universal Music Group labels") as a result of the song having received over five million streams.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-UMS_Platinum-1) The song entered the _[Svensktoppen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Svensktoppen "Svensktoppen")_ track lists.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-swedishcharts1-19) In July 2013, at _[Sommarkrysset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sommarkrysset "Sommarkrysset")_ in [Gröna Lund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gr%C3%B6na_Lund "Gröna Lund"), she received a 3× platinum award for _Introducing_ for selling over 120,000 copies in Sweden.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Introducing_certified_triple_platinum-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-24)

On 27 March 2013, Larsson's next EP was revealed through a music video of "She's Not Me (Pt. 1)" on YouTube.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Next_EP_album_YouTube-25) The five-song EP, _[Allow Me to Reintroduce Myself](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allow\_Me\_to\_Reintroduce\_Myself\_(EP) "Allow Me to Reintroduce Myself (EP)")_, was released in Scandinavia on 5 July 2013.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Allow_Me_To_Reintroduce_Myself_release_date-26) "[She's Not Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She%27s_Not_Me "She's Not Me")" (consisting of "She's Not Me (Pt. 1)" and "She's Not Me (Pt. 2)") was released as a double-single on 25 June 2013.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Allow_Me_To_Reintroduce_Myself_release_date-26) On 3 April 2013, Larsson revealed on her blog that she had signed a three-year contract with [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records") in the United States.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Signed_with_Epic-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-3-year_contract_with_Epic-28) On 11 December 2013, Larsson performed at the [Nobel Peace Prize Concert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize_Concert "Nobel Peace Prize Concert") in Oslo.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-29) On 1 October 2014, Larsson released her Scandinavian debut studio album _[1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "1 (Zara Larsson album)")_, including the songs "Uncover", "[Bad Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_Boys_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Bad Boys (Zara Larsson song)")" and "She's Not Me" (Pt. 1 and Pt. 2), in Scandinavia. The version of "Uncover" in the album was a newer recording by Larsson from 2014. The album went platinum in Sweden. Larsson was an opening act for English singer [Cher Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cher_Lloyd "Cher Lloyd")'s [I Wish Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Wish_Tour "I Wish Tour").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-posh24-30)

### 2015–2017: _So Good_ and international success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zara_Larsson&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2015–2017: So Good and international success")]

On 15 January 2015, Larsson released [_Uncover_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncover_(EP) "Uncover (EP)"), her first international EP, containing songs from her album _[1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "1 (Zara Larsson album)")_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-31)

On 5 June 2015, Larsson released the single "[Lush Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lush_Life_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Lush Life (Zara Larsson song)")" from her upcoming second studio album. The song became her second number one single and was certified 4× platinum in Sweden. The song reached the top five in 18 countries and was certified platinum in 16 countries.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-34) On 22 July 2015, Larsson released her collaboration with English singer [MNEK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MNEK "MNEK"), "[Never Forget You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Forget_You_(Zara_Larsson_and_MNEK_song) "Never Forget You (Zara Larsson and MNEK song)")", the second single from her upcoming album.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-35) The song reached number one in Sweden, number three in Australia,[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-36) and number five in the United Kingdom.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-37)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-swedishcharts1-19) The song was certified platinum in Sweden after two weeks.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-38)

[![Image 4: Zara Larsson, a Swedish singer, sings into a black microphone with both hands, while wearing a pink top with translucent sleeves and light blue painted nails](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Zara_Larsson_Stavernfestivalen_%28203836%29.jpg/250px-Zara_Larsson_Stavernfestivalen_%28203836%29.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zara_Larsson_Stavernfestivalen_(203836).jpg)

Larsson during [Stavernfestivalen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stavernfestivalen "Stavernfestivalen"), 2016

In February 2016, [Tinie Tempah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tinie_Tempah "Tinie Tempah") released "[Girls Like](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girls_Like "Girls Like")" featuring Larsson.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-39) Larsson was later featured in the official song of [UEFA Euro 2016](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2016 "UEFA Euro 2016"), [David Guetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Guetta "David Guetta")'s "[This One's for You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_One%27s_for_You_(David_Guetta_song) "This One's for You (David Guetta song)")".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-40)

On 1 September 2016, Larsson released "[Ain't My Fault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ain%27t_My_Fault_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Ain't My Fault (Zara Larsson song)")", the third single from her upcoming album.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-41) On 22 October 2016, Larsson was named one of _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_'s "30 Most Influential Teens of 2016".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-42) She released "[I Would Like](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Would_Like "I Would Like")", the fourth single from her upcoming album, on 11 November 2016.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-43) It peaked at number two in the United Kingdom[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-44) and at number four in Sweden.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-45)

In January 2017, Larsson released "[So Good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Good_(Zara_Larsson_song) "So Good (Zara Larsson song)")", featuring American singer [Ty Dolla Sign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign"). The single served as the fifth single from her second album [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/So_Good_(Zara_Larsson_album) "So Good (Zara Larsson album)"), which was released on 17 March 2017 as her first international album.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-46) The album also features a collaboration with [Wizkid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wizkid_(musician) "Wizkid (musician)") titled "Sundown".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-47) "[Symphony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphony_(Clean_Bandit_song) "Symphony (Clean Bandit song)")" by [Clean Bandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Bandit "Clean Bandit") featuring Larsson was included as a bonus track and was released as a single on the same date and became Larsson's fifth number one single in her home country[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-48) and first number one single in the United Kingdom.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-49) The album became her second number one album in Sweden and peaked in the top ten in Australia, Denmark, Finland, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-50) and the United Kingdom.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-51)

On 12 May 2017, Larsson released a music video for "[Don't Let Me Be Yours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don%27t_Let_Me_Be_Yours "Don't Let Me Be Yours")" as the sixth single from _So Good_,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-52) with "[Only You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_You_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Only You (Zara Larsson song)")" being released as the seventh single from the album on 11 August 2017.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-53)

### 2017–2022: _Poster Girl_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zara_Larsson&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2017–2022: Poster Girl")]

[![Image 5: Zara Larsson performs onstage in a white and black patterned jacket, a light purple tube top, and white pants, waving to the crowd with a microphone in her hand](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/62/Zara_Larsson_-_Ilosaarirock_2018_-_17.jpg/250px-Zara_Larsson_-_Ilosaarirock_2018_-_17.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Zara_Larsson_-_Ilosaarirock_2018_-_17.jpg)

Larsson performing at the [Ilosaarirock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilosaarirock "Ilosaarirock") festival in July 2018

In September 2017, Larsson announced that she had started working on her third studio album, saying in an interview she had written two new songs with MNEK. On 11 December 2017, Larsson once again performed at the Nobel Peace Prize Concert, this time alongside American singer [John Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Legend "John Legend").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-54)

In January 2018, Larsson was named to _[Forbes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes "Forbes")_' "[30 Under 30 Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forbes_30_Under_30 "Forbes 30 Under 30")" list in the entertainment category.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-55)

In September 2018, Larsson announced the lead single from her third studio album, "[Ruin My Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruin_My_Life "Ruin My Life")". She released the song and music video on 18 October 2018. The track was commercially successful worldwide, being certified at least gold in the US and the UK, while reaching number one in the Netherlands. In 2019, Larsson released the follow-up singles "[Don't Worry Bout Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don%27t_Worry_Bout_Me_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Don't Worry Bout Me (Zara Larsson song)")" and "[All the Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Time_(Zara_Larsson_song) "All the Time (Zara Larsson song)")", as well as the then promotional single "[Wow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wow_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Wow (Zara Larsson song)")".[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-58)

In January 2019, she was featured on the song "[Holding Out for You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holding_Out_for_You "Holding Out for You")" by Italian rapper and singer [Fedez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fedez "Fedez").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-59) On 8 November 2019, Larsson's next single, "[Invisible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invisible_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Invisible (Zara Larsson song)")", taken from the 2019 movie _[Klaus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klaus\_(film) "Klaus (film)")_, the first original animated feature film released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"), was released on the same day the film was released.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Invisible_announcement_Epic-60)

In March 2020, Larsson was featured on [Kygo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kygo "Kygo")'s single, "[Like It Is](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Like_It_Is_(song) "Like It Is (song)")", alongside American rapper [Tyga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyga "Tyga"). The song has performed moderately well, becoming a top-five song in Sweden, New Zealand, and Norway.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In June 2020, Larsson announced the single "[Love Me Land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_Me_Land "Love Me Land")" through Instagram. She released the song and music video on 10 July 2020. On the same day, an interview with her and [Sveriges Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Radio "Sveriges Radio") was published. She announced that her new album would be released after 2020. She also said: "I am prepared in a completely different way. I have the next song ready, album cover, the video, the album is done. I just feel ready in a different way." It was then revealed on her [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") page that the album would be called _Love Me Land_ and that the title track was the first single from the album.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-61) However, Larsson later clarified in an interview that the album is titled _[Poster Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poster\_Girl\_(album) "Poster Girl (album)")_ and that "Wow" would also be included on the album,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-wow-62) after officially announcing it as a single on 26 August 2020.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-63)

In September 2020, Larsson released a remix of "Wow" featuring American singer [Sabrina Carpenter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabrina_Carpenter "Sabrina Carpenter").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-64)

On 8 January 2021, she released "[Talk About Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_About_Love_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Talk About Love (Zara Larsson song)")" featuring American rapper [Young Thug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Thug "Young Thug") as the third single from _Poster Girl_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

_[Poster Girl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poster\_Girl\_(album) "Poster Girl (album)")_ was released on 5 March 2021[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Idolator_PG-65) to positive reviews. The album performed moderately commercially, debuting at number three on the [Swedish Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sverigetopplistan "Sverigetopplistan"), 12 on the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"), and 170 on the US [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200").

On 21 May 2021, Larsson released a summer edition of _Poster Girl_.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-66) She also performed songs at a virtual party on [Roblox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roblox "Roblox") to celebrate her new album.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-67)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-68)

On 22 April 2022, Larsson released "[Words](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Words_(Alesso_song) "Words (Alesso song)")" with Swedish DJ [Alesso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alesso "Alesso").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-69) The song was a moderate success in Europe, reaching the top five in Sweden and the top 40 in Flanders, Croatia, Hungary, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland and the United Kingdom.

In June 2022, Larsson announced that she had left [TEN Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TEN_Music_Group "TEN Music Group") to start her own record label named _Sommer House_ and acquired ownership over her musical catalog in the process. She also renewed her contract with [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records") with all future releases from then on being released under her own label _Sommer House_ under exclusive license to [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records") in the US and be distributed by [Sony Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music") in Sweden.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-70)

### 2023–present: _Venus_ and _Midnight Sun_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zara_Larsson&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2023–present: Venus and Midnight Sun")]

On 27 January 2023, Larsson released "[Can't Tame Her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can%27t_Tame_Her "Can't Tame Her")", the lead single from her fourth studio album, _[Venus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venus\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "Venus (Zara Larsson album)")_.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-The_Line_of_Best_Fit-71) Subsequently, she released "[End of Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/End_of_Time_(Zara_Larsson_song) "End of Time (Zara Larsson song)")" on 19 May 2023 as the second single from the album.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-72) The third single from the album, "[On My Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_My_Love "On My Love")", was released on 15 September 2023 in collaboration with French DJ [David Guetta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Guetta "David Guetta"). On 26 October 2023, Larsson officially announced _Venus_ and made it available for pre-order.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-74) On the same day, she also revealed the _Venus Tour,_ a European headlining tour in support of the album, set to begin in February 2024.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-75) On 1 December 2023, Larsson released her holiday EP _[Honor the Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor\_the\_Light "Honor the Light")_.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-76) On 19 January 2024, "[You Love Who You Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You_Love_Who_You_Love "You Love Who You Love")" was released as the fourth single from the album.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-77)_Venus_ was released on 9 February 2024 to generally positive reviews from critics.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-79) On 3 April 2024, Larsson released a streamed concert, _Venus Tour_, recorded at [AFAS Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFAS_Live "AFAS Live") in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam") and released via the [pay-per-view](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pay-per-view "Pay-per-view") platform [_On Air_.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_Air_(streaming_service) "On Air (streaming service)")[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-80)

On 15 May 2023, Netflix Nordic's official Twitter account announced a new film called _[A Part of You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Part\_of\_You "A Part of You"),_ which was then released on 31 May 2024.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-81) The main cast consists of Larsson, Felicia Maxime and [Edvin Ryding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edvin_Ryding "Edvin Ryding").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-82)

On 25 April 2025, Larsson released "[Pretty Ugly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pretty_Ugly_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Pretty Ugly (Zara Larsson song)")", the lead single from her fifth studio album, _[Midnight Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Sun\_(Zara\_Larsson\_album) "Midnight Sun (Zara Larsson album)")_.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-83) The [title track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_Sun_(Zara_Larsson_song) "Midnight Sun (Zara Larsson song)") was released on 13 June 2025 as the second single from the album and received a nomination for [Best Dance Pop Recording](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Dance_Pop_Recording "Grammy Award for Best Dance Pop Recording") at [68th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/68th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "68th Annual Grammy Awards"), becoming Larsson's first Grammy nomination.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-85) The album was released on 26 September 2025. Larsson joined [Tate McRae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tate_McRae "Tate McRae") as a supporting act on the North American leg of the [Miss Possessive Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Possessive_Tour "Miss Possessive Tour") from August to September 2025 before embarking on the [Midnight Sun Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_Sun_Tour "Midnight Sun Tour") in October 2025. [[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-87)

In 2015, Larsson planned and hosted a summer speech broadcast on [Sveriges Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Radio "Sveriges Radio"), one of 58 celebrities that year. The 48-minute speech was broadcast live on the [P1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sveriges_Radio_P1 "Sveriges Radio P1") channel on 25 July 2015, at 13:00 [CET](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_European_Time "Central European Time").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-2015_summer_speech-10) Larsson was 17 at the time, which made her the youngest such speaker, surpassing [Robyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robyn "Robyn") and [Gina Dirawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gina_Dirawi "Gina Dirawi") at age 20.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-88) In the speech, she talked about her life, her music career, her [feminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminism "Feminism") views, others' reactions to her, and her feelings about all of it.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-2015_summer_speech-10)

Between 2017 and 2019, she dated English model Brian H. Whittaker, whom she [tweeted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") in 2015, but did not meet until two years later.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-89) Since 2020, Larsson has been in a relationship with Swedish dancer Lamin Holmén.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-90)

On 18 May 2017, Larsson released an [H&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%26M "H&M") collection containing various garments and accessories.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-:0-92) She was involved in the creation process by making decisions about press, colors and fitting. Pink is the common color throughout the entire collection.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-:0-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-93)

Larsson has grown increasingly vocal with her views on other artists and industry workers with whom she works and admires. While she has high praise for performers such as [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé"),[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-harpers-94) she is equal in her opposing views of such artists as [Dr. Luke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Luke "Dr. Luke")[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-nme-95) and [Chris Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Brown "Chris Brown").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-96) Larsson, a fan of Beyoncé, identifies as a [feminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feminism "Feminism") and models herself an "activist" after the singer. She attributes her openness of opinion on social media and in interviews to her parents, claiming: "Both my parents are very educated when it comes to social issues and being [woke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woke "Woke") about what's going on in the world, and they've been very supportive of me having a voice".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-harpers-94)

In January 2015, Larsson gained a lot of positive attention in Sweden and the United States after posting a picture on her [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") showing a condom wrapped around her leg and foot to refute the idea that penises can be too big for condoms to fit around.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Condom_news-97) She has since 2019 been fronting a new campaign from [Durex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durex "Durex") and [AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AIDS "AIDS") organization (RED) promoting sexual health awareness and raising money for AIDS treatment in South Africa.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-98) In order to increase public understanding of incontinence, she has openly stated that she used diapers until she was seven years old.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-99)

In June 2015, she came into the spotlight in her home country for openly questioning whether the [Bråvalla Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Br%C3%A5valla_Festival "Bråvalla Festival") had any gender perspective whatsoever, as its promotion and performance line-up were highly dominated by male artists. She also wondered why she wasn't presented among the main acts despite being the most popular artist on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") of the festival's acts. That same day, Swedish singer [Günther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%BCnther_(singer) "Günther (singer)") wrote on his [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") profile criticizing Larsson: "You are one of many [teenybopper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenybopper "Teenybopper") chicks who are world-famous in Sweden and maximally hyped but don't come with any hits, only a lot of fuss". During her performance at the festival she countered back saying: "Fuck Günther, fuck all woman haters". This led to the hashtag #backazara being created and popularised on social media platforms, where thousands of people, including famous Swedish people, showed their support for Larsson.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-Br%C3%A5valla_1-100)

On 11 May 2021, Larsson posted an image of text on her [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") where she criticised Israel for killing Palestinian civilians and upholding [apartheid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartheid "Apartheid"), while expressing the importance of standing against [antisemitism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism "Antisemitism").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-101) In the [2022 Swedish general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Swedish_general_election "2022 Swedish general election"), she publicly endorsed the [Left Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_Party_(Sweden) "Left Party (Sweden)").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-102) Additionally, Larsson has expressed opposition to [toxic masculinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toxic_masculinity "Toxic masculinity").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-theguardian.com-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-105)

At the outbreak of the [Gaza War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_war "Gaza war") in October 2023, Larsson shared an image to her Instagram story with the caption “Oh so it’s stand with Ukraine when Russia invades but not Palesti-”.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-106) After receiving backlash, she issued an apology for her comments, stating “My comment on the war i previously had on my story has got a lot of valid criticism thinking I’m in support of terrorists. Let me just be clear – I have never and will never support terrorists. It was badly worded and thoughtlessly posted and for that I apologize.”[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-107) However, in the same apology, she reaffirmed her support for Palestinian civilians.

In March 2019, it was announced that Larsson had started a commercial cooperation with Chinese technology company [Huawei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei "Huawei").[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-108) Larsson's cooperation with Huawei was criticised by experts on human rights in China and others, who referred to Huawei's close ties to the authoritarian [Chinese government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_China "Government of China") and its [record on human rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_rights_in_China "Human rights in China").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-109) In August 2020, Larsson announced that she had terminated her cooperation with Huawei, stating that China is "not a nice state" and that she does not stand behind its policies.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-110) In response, Huawei stated that the endorsement deal was time-limited and had already ended in 2019.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-111) Larsson's music was reportedly taken down from [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") in China less than a week after her comments.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-112)

Artistry and influences
-----------------------

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Zara_Larsson&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Artistry and influences")]

Larsson is mainly a [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") singer. She has experimented with [electropop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electropop "Electropop"),[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-113)[house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_music "House music"),[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-114) and [dance music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance_music "Dance music").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-115)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-116) Additionally, she is influenced by [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R%26B "Contemporary R&B").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-117)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-118) Vocally, she has described herself as a [soprano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soprano "Soprano").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-119)

She has cited [Beyoncé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") as her biggest musical influence.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-120) Larsson's Swedish influences include [Robyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robyn "Robyn"), [Seinabo Sey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seinabo_Sey "Seinabo Sey"), [Sabina Ddumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabina_Ddumba "Sabina Ddumba") and her sister Hanna Larsson, with her [neo soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo_soul "Neo soul") group Lennixx.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-121) Her additional international influences include [Christina Aguilera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Aguilera "Christina Aguilera"), [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna") and [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga").[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-122)[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zara_Larsson#cite_note-auto-123)

6.content:
![Image 1: A black background with white text

Description automatically generated](https://www.sonymusic.ca/press_release/image/png;base64,)

**ZARA LARSSON RELEASES NEW ALBUM**[**_MIDNIGHT SUN_**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fzaralarsson.lnk.to%2FMidnightSun&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151112766%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=q46xx0r69mHHpf6lH2KLDNH5QE2EThFJLm%2FOcpnM0Wc%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://zaralarsson.lnk.to/MidnightSun. Click or tap if you trust this link.")

**HIGHLY ANTICIPATED BODY OF WORK FEATURES NEW SONGS “BLUE MOON,” “HOT & SEXY” AND MORE, PLUS ACCLAIMED SINGLES “PRETTY UGLY,” “CRUSH” AND “MIDNIGHT SUN”**

**NORTH AMERICAN HEADLINE TOUR SET FOR FEBRUARY – APRIL 2026**

![Image 2: ZARA LARSSON RELEASES NEW ALBUM MIDNIGHT SUN](https://cdn-p.smehost.net/sites/a6700d2fbaf642099802a57af8b10fe6/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Zara-Larsson-1.png)

**(Toronto, ON — September 26,2025)**It may be the first week of fall, but for**Zara Larsson,**summer never ends. Today, the multiplatinum chart-topping global pop powerhouse releases her hotly anticipated new album,**_Midnight Sun_**. Get it[**HERE**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fzaralarsson.lnk.to%2FMidnightSun&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151150296%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=HSa9NHAxeP0427kqzr%2FYD8UHzbpP4c8E5Fx9Z88XbBA%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://zaralarsson.lnk.to/MidnightSun. Click or tap if you trust this link.")at all DSPs via**Sommer House**/**Epic Records**.

Unapologetically unfiltered and openly vulnerable, the 10-track set ripples with personal confidence and is set to a bold mix of kaleidoscopic pop and euphoric dance that complements**Zara**’s every mood. Plumbing the depths of her artistry and journey over nearly 20 years in the public eye, the album is unafraid to show all sides of the 27-year-old: lovestruck, wistful, ambitious, cocky, flippant, and uncertain, often in the same breath.

Also available today is the exclusive**_Midnight Sun (Lisa Frank Edition)_**CD, a vibrant collaboration with the iconic design brand**Lisa Frank, Inc**. The limited-run package brings to life a dreamy, aquatic world inspired by the memes and moments that so many of**Zara**’s fans around the world participated in over the past year.Get it while supplies last[**HERE**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fzaralarsson.lnk.to%2FLisaFrank&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151172884%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=KQn1sHFAHFQafqk0sR3evnXwR8F2UhiHaWD3AwWuBzo%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://zaralarsson.lnk.to/LisaFrank. Click or tap if you trust this link.").

The album arrives as**Zara**approaches the finale of her arena-conquering run on**Tate McCrae**’s**Miss Possessive Tour**with back-to-back nights at**Los Angeles’ Kia Forum**starting tonight. As _Billboard_ proclaimed after a two-night run at**New York’s Madison Square Garden**, the tour has proven that**Zara’s**“_Stateside domination seems all but certain.”_ With that, she’ll headline her own**Midnight Sun Tour**starting in**Europe**this fall, with recently announced**North America**dates to follow starting in February 2026.See her global touring itinerary below go[**HERE**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.zaralarssonofficial.com%2F&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151189362%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=fu4PitMgjsRhRDIChzROEzLLt7UJcHtlGeTIZLVV4CU%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: http://www.zaralarssonofficial.com/. Click or tap if you trust this link.")for tickets.

The headline tour will bring to life her most emotionally evocative and viscerally thrilling set of songs yet on**_Midnight Sun_**, which she crafted over the last year alongside songwriter**Helena Gao**and producers**MNEK**,**Margo XS**, and**Zhone.**

The previously unheard**“Blue Moon”**is an anthem for the hopeless romantics set to warm tones and heart-racing drum ’n’ bass rhythms — a celebration of timeless love. At the other end of the spectrum is**“Hot & Sexy,”**a mix of ’80s electro, ’90s house, Y2K pop, and 2010s bass music that samples**Tiffany Pollard**’s iconic _Big Brother_ rant – a charged-up “no boys allowed” anthem that evolves into a hyperpop fever dream with lyrics that dig deep beneath the surface and explore autonomy. On the introspective penultimate track “**Saturn’s Return**,”**Zara**reflects on personal growth and self-discovery, embracing uncertainty with a deeper sense of self. Paired with “**The Ambition**” right before, which explores the double-edged nature of drive and the pressures of success in modern times, the two highlight the album’s raw honesty as they explore identity, expectations, and stepping into a new era of life.

**_Midnight Sun_**’s robust set of new songs join already thriving singles like**“**[**Crush**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DZB600rRlPO8&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151204507%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=8Fvgy30ss6y7fUGbCiAR%2BKzqYWMXcIsRflNY5zBoge8%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZB600rRlPO8. Click or tap if you trust this link.")**,”**which was one of the most-added at US Top 40 radio six weeks in a row, where it is currently Top 25 on the Mediabase Pop chart and pushing Top 10 on the Mediabase Dance Radio chart.The era kicked off with the unabashedly rowdy**“**[**Pretty Ugly**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DPaddtn5IdCk&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151219599%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=5gjYmmuwJY20Xahw1nH8PuC%2BC7mku%2F3BStYRSjcUGHM%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Paddtn5IdCk. Click or tap if you trust this link.")**”**whose**Charlotte Rutherford**-directed,**Zoi Tatopoulos-**choreographed video was nominated at the 2025 MTV Video Music Awards for “Best Choreography.” And then there’s the transcendent title track,**“**[**Midnight Sun**](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3DuvY8fdgezLQ%26t%3D1s&data=05%7C02%7Chansel.adukwarko%40sonymusic.com%7C06306560f3d64c6cbecf08ddfd163af7%7Cf0aff3b791a54aaeaf71c63e1dda2049%7C0%7C0%7C638944994151234328%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=08w2oGZa%2Bo0nAujIMSfk1lSLfettwKYYYu%2BpYy3t36M%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uvY8fdgezLQ&t=1s. Click or tap if you trust this link.")**,”**which has been viral all summer long thanks to**Charlotte Rutherford**’s Y2K-inspired music video and**Zara**’s jaw-dropping vocal prowess. With cosigns from a wide array of fellow artists like Renee Rapp, PinkPanthress and Ariana Grande, the press has rallied around the track, with _Rolling Stone_ calling it a _“song-of-the-summer contender”_ right out of the gate._PAPER dubbed it_ a _“shimmering pop anthem soaked in nostalgia,”_ while _GRAMMY.com_ wrote _“the beat drops with such hypnotic force that the track’s climax feels like staring directly into, well, a midnight sun.”_**_Pitchfork_**, however, summed up what we are all thinking: “_Midnight Sun is simply too much my shit!”_

_“Throughout Midnight Sun,”_**Zara****Larsson**says, “_I get to just capture that total Scandinavian vibe, which is something that I have grown up with—it’s a huge part of me, my happiest memories and my saddest ones, too. A part of my soul is a Swedish summer night. This record encompasses that.”_

Now, as the fires of anticipation reach a blinding blaze,**Zara Larsson**’s never-ending**_Midnight Sun_**is, at last, here — and here to stay.

_“It just feels like me—knowing myself, this album is just really, really me. And also,”_**Zara**says with a grin, “_No one can do me the way I can.”_
